title: Sports Store — Kubernetes manifests (starter)
summary: Starter guide for the Stage 3 local Kubernetes manifests: directory layout, internal service DNS constraint, suggested kubectl/helm apply order, and the branching convention.
scope: app-secrets (JWT_SECRET, per-service MONGO_URI, mongo root creds)
MongoDB via Bitnami Helm chart (values.yaml, init-configmap.yaml)
git branching convention and PR ruleset

STALENESS: document describes a Stage 3 starter state where every manifest holds inline TODO comments instead of working resource definitions; repo is now GitOps-managed with real per-service image tags, so the starter framing is likely stale relative to STATUS.md
constraints: Namespace must remain `sports-store` — later stages (Helm chart, EKS deploy, CI/CD, Argo CD, observability) all assume that name; do not rename.
Each backend Service `metadata.name` must match the hostnames used in `gateway/nginx.conf` `proxy_pass` lines (carried over from Stage 2 Compose aliases), or the gateway fails DNS resolution.
Changing a backend hostname requires updating the matching `proxy_pass` line in `gateway/nginx.conf` and rebuilding the gateway image.
Only the `gateway` Service may be externally reachable (NodePort/LoadBalancer/Ingress); all other Services stay ClusterIP.
Secrets must be applied before MongoDB values and app Deployments, since all of them reference `app-secrets`.
MongoDB must be healthy before app Deployments connect; ordering must come from retry-friendly app startup or an initContainer, not readinessProbe alone, and the chosen approach must be documented.
All changes land on `main` via pull request with at least 1 approval, enforced by repository ruleset.
notes: Type taken from manifest (DOC), not heuristics; content signals agree — prose guide with layout, apply-order runbook, and conventions, no decision record, user stories, or API contracts.
